lead: A flywheel is a rotating store of kinetic energy. An engine or press delivers torque in pulses; the flywheel gives energy back between pulses and keeps speed nearly steady. A solid disk uses its whole mass; a rimmed wheel puts most mass in a thin rim at large radius, so it stores more energy for the same mass. Flywheels smooth speed in punch presses, IC engines, steam engines and rolling mills.
prereq: You need Unit 1 for centrifugal force and thin-ring stress, and chapter 4.7 for another energy-storing spring.

blocks.text: Let ω be the mean angular speed in rad/s. The wheel runs between ω₁ and ω₂. The coefficient of fluctuation of speed is C<sub>s</sub> = (ω₁ − ω₂)/ω. It is dimensionless. A small C<sub>s</sub> means tight speed control.

blocks.where: ω₁ is maximum angular speed in rad/s; ω₂ is minimum angular speed in rad/s; ω = (ω₁ + ω₂)/2 is mean angular speed in rad/s.
ΔE is energy fluctuation per cycle in J; I is mass moment of inertia in kg·m²; ω is mean angular speed in rad/s; C<sub>s</sub> is the speed-fluctuation coefficient.

blocks.text: This follows from ΔE = ½I(ω₁² − ω₂²) = Iω(ω₁ − ω₂) = Iω²C<sub>s</sub>. To size a wheel: find ω; choose C<sub>s</sub> for the duty; compute I; choose geometry; compute mass; check stress. Presses use a large ΔE for one stroke, so I is large.
Solid disk: I = ½ m r². Rimmed thin rim: I ≈ m r².
blocks.where: m is mass in kg; r is outer radius for a solid disk and mean rim radius for a rimmed wheel, in m. Hub and arm inertia are usually neglected.

items: A solid disk is compact but gives less I for the same mass.
A rimmed wheel gives high I per kg because the rim sits at large r. Some syllabi call it a spoked flywheel.
Do not use ½mr² for a rimmed wheel unless the wheel really is a solid disk.

blocks.text: At rim speed v = ωr, every rim element has outward centrifugal force. For a free thin ring this gives hoop stress σ = ρv². It does not depend on rim thickness. In engines the rim also sees torque pulses; in presses it releases a large energy burst.
σ = ρ v², with v = ω r
blocks.where: σ is hoop stress in Pa; ρ is density in kg/m³; v is rim speed in m/s; r is mean rim radius in m; ω is angular speed in rad/s.

blocks.text: Cast iron has ρ ≈ 7200 kg/m³. A rim at 40 m/s reaches σ ≈ 11.5 MPa; at 80 m/s it reaches σ ≈ 46 MPa. Stress rises with speed squared, so the safe speed limit is set by the rim material, not by torque alone.

Arms carry torque T from hub to rim. With n arms, the tangential force per arm at the rim is F = T/(n r). Treat an arm as a cantilever of length r. Its bending moment at the hub is M = F r = T/n, and bending stress is σ<sub>b</sub> = M c / I<sub>arm</sub>. Arms also feel centrifugal tension; check σ<sub>t</sub> = F<sub>c</sub>/A.
M = T/n,  σ<sub>b</sub> = M c / I<sub>arm</sub>,  F<sub>c</sub> = m<sub>arm</sub> ω² r<sub>g</sub>
blocks.where: T is torque in N·m; n is number of arms; c is distance from arm neutral axis to outer fibre in m; I<sub>arm</sub> is second moment of the arm section in m⁴; m<sub>arm</sub> is mass of one arm in kg; r<sub>g</sub> is its centroid radius in m; A is arm cross-section area in m².

figure.caption: Follow the chain from energy per cycle to hoop stress. The values are the worked example: a cast-iron rim at 37.7 m/s reaches about 10.2 MPa.

spec.title: Rimmed flywheel check
spec.aria: The energy fluctuation and mean speed give inertia, then rim mass and rim speed give the centrifugal hoop stress.

examples.question: A rimmed flywheel absorbs ΔE = 15 kJ per cycle at mean speed N = 600 rpm with C<sub>s</sub> = 0.05. The rim mean radius is r = 0.6 m and cast-iron density is ρ = 7200 kg/m³. Find the inertia, rim mass, rim speed and hoop stress.
examples.answer: I = 76.0 kg·m², m = 211.1 kg, v = 37.7 m/s and σ = 10.2 MPa.
examples.check:
import math
dE = 15000.0
N = 600.0
Cs = 0.05
r = 0.6
rho = 7200.0
omega = 2*math.pi*N/60
I = dE/(omega**2*Cs)
m = I/r**2
v = omega*r
sigma = rho*v**2
print(round(I,1))
print(round(m,1))
print(round(v,1))
print(round(sigma/1e6,1))

traps: Using diameter in place of radius in m = I/r² and v = ωr. Use the mean radius.
Using the full speed change ω₁ − ω₂ as C<sub>s</sub>. C<sub>s</sub> is already divided by mean speed ω.
Using I = ½mr² for a rimmed flywheel. That is the solid-disk value; use I ≈ mr² for a thin rim.
Leaving ΔE in kJ or N in rpm. Convert to J and rad/s before substitution.
Treating σ = ρv² as a complete arm-and-rim design. It is the free thin-ring hoop stress; arms need their own bending and centrifugal checks.

quiz.q: Define the coefficient of fluctuation of speed.
quiz.a: C<sub>s</sub> = (ω₁ − ω₂)/ω, where ω₁ and ω₂ are maximum and minimum angular speeds and ω is the mean angular speed.

quiz.q: Why does a rimmed wheel store more energy per kg than a solid disk of the same outer radius?
quiz.a: Most mass sits at the mean rim radius, so I ≈ mr². A solid disk has I = ½mr², with much mass near the axis; for the same mass and radius the rim gives about twice the inertia.

quiz.q: A flywheel absorbs ΔE = 8 kJ per cycle at ω = 50 rad/s with C<sub>s</sub> = 0.04. Find I.
A cast-iron rim has mean radius 0.5 m and runs at 900 rpm. Take ρ = 7200 kg/m³. Find rim speed and hoop stress.
Why can a rimmed flywheel fail at high speed even when it transmits little torque?
quiz.a: The rim's own centrifugal force causes hoop stress σ = ρv². This grows with speed squared and does not depend on the transmitted torque; at high v the rim can burst even at light load.

quiz.q: A flywheel has n arms carrying torque T at rim radius r. What happens to arm bending stress if n is doubled, all else unchanged?
quiz.a: Force per arm is F = T/(nr), so M = Fr = T/n. Doubling n halves M and halves bending stress, if the arm section is unchanged.

quiz.q: State two duties of a flywheel in an engine or press.
quiz.a: Store kinetic energy between power pulses and reduce speed fluctuation during each cycle.

beyond: Not for the exam. Production flywheels are checked by finite element analysis for rim, arm and hub stress, and burst containment is tested for safety. Composite rims can reach higher tip speed than cast iron because ρ is lower while strength is high. Search terms: flywheel energy storage, burst speed, composite flywheel, rim hoop stress.
